content.title: About
content.content: Boston lettuce is a crisp, light‑green leafy vegetable cultivated in the United States. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and firm yet tender leaves. Boston lettuce is commonly used in fresh salads, sandwiches, and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Boston lettuce belongs to the Asteraceae family and is a variety of leaf lettuce.
It was named after the city of Boston, where it was first commercially developed in the early 20th century.
Its leaves are generally denser and less fragile than those of romaine or iceberg lettuce.
Boston lettuce is often grown in greenhouses, allowing year‑round production.
It is composed of more than 95 % water, making it an excellent source of hydration.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Boston lettuce provides a high amount of vitamin K, which is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate supports normal cell division and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Its calorie content is very low, making it a great choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: The leaves contain carotenoids and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to leafy vegetables, including lettuce.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw lettuce can be contaminated with gut bacteria such as E. coli, so thorough washing is essential.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional production may involve chemical pesticides; choosing organic or washing well reduces exposure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boston lettuce is typically eaten raw: in fresh salads, as part of sandwiches, in wraps, or as a side to meat dishes. Leaves can be torn by hand or sliced. For extra crispness, rinse them in cold water and spin dry in a salad spinner.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Boston lettuce in the refrigerator in a slightly damp bag or a container with ventilation holes. Use within 3–5 days. Discard any leaves that become yellowed or limp.
